_why: FIFTH held-out batch. Never used to choose or tune a change.
M53 was measured and NOT merged (see M53 and M55 in the learning log),
so on the shipped code these questions are a record of a known gap.
Written for M53, after its code but before any model run of it. M53
splits the facts' one `condition` into the condition the claim is for
(`claimed_condition`) and any other the person mentions
(`other_conditions`), and lets code settle 'pre-existing: yes' only when
the person's words date the CLAIMED condition. Every case here mentions a
medical history; in some the claim is for that history, in others for
something new. The first case is the question from M51 (Failure 119)
that a 'yes' rule refused under the diabetes wait.
Same synthetic policy and conventions as scenarios.json. Same author as
the fix, so not fully independent.

cases.scenario: I have had diabetes for years. I took out this policy last month and was admitted for a broken arm after a fall.
cases.why: The claim is for an injury from a fall, not for the diabetes. The pre-existing disease wait concerns only the diabetes, and the initial 30-day wait excepts accidents.

cases.scenario: I have had asthma since I was a child. I have held this policy for a year and was admitted for appendicitis.
cases.why: Appendicitis is the claim and nothing dates it before the policy; the childhood asthma is history the claim is not for. A year clears the initial wait.

cases.scenario: I have suffered from high blood pressure for years, and eight months after I bought this policy I was admitted because of it.
cases.why: The claim is for the blood pressure itself, which the person has had for years - longer than eight months of cover - so it predates the policy, and eight months is short of the 36-month pre-existing disease wait.

cases.scenario: My thyroid problem began long before I took out this policy. I have held it for 14 months and was admitted with dengue fever.
cases.why: Dengue is the claim, caught under cover; the thyroid problem is history the claim is not for.

cases.scenario: I have suffered from migraines for years and was admitted for pneumonia six months after buying this policy.
cases.why: History and claim in one sentence: the migraines are old, the pneumonia is the claim and is not described as existing before the policy.
